grh_d184526bb851184930bf.title: Baby On Doorstep
paragraphs: An unidentified infant is left on Dr. Christian's doorstep with no note or label. Although several experienced mothers offer to adopt him, the bachelor doctor decides to keep the baby himself until the person with the strongest claim appears, and over the next six months he and Judy become deeply attached to the child. One day Lila Bronson, a woman Dr. Christian knew when she was younger, comes in with a sprained ankle. The doctor notices that her toes overlap in the same distinctive way as the baby's, and when she hears the child and asks to see him her emotional reaction confirms what he suspects. Lila has returned for the son she abandoned. Rather than accuse or shame her, Dr. Christian asks whether she would like to adopt the baby and raise him as her own, quietly restoring mother and child while admitting he knew that if he waited long enough the right person would come back.

grh_d1086969e0b96286ee2b.title: The Camberwell Poisoning
paragraphs: After Gerald Lovelace is found with his skull crushed and cyanide injected into his wrist, Holmes must choose among relatives whose alibis leave different possible times of death. The key is Gerald's meticulously wound watch: Holmes finds one turn missing, later establishes that each turn represents two hours, and fixes the murder at 11 p.m., when only the childlike Gilly had the opportunity. Gilly then innocently describes the exact method without having been told it, explaining that Gerald had planned to use the poison on his beloved old dog Gladstone. Gilly killed Gerald to protect the dog and is sent to private care rather than tried.

grh_d18b32aadeed44f0e043.title: Words at War 43-11-30 (25) Ave Duce - Sawdust Caesar - Balcony Empire
paragraphs: A satirical radio treatment of Mussolini and Italian fascism, based on Fruits of Fascism, Sawdust Caesar and Balcony Empire, lets the personified city of Rome address the fallen dictator directly. The program traces fascism's rise through intimidation, Blackshirt violence, the March on Rome, propaganda and the gradual destruction of elections, free speech and independent institutions. Rome mocks Mussolini's betrayals of the people, monarchy and church and ends by portraying Allied advance and Nazi occupation as signs that his promised empire has collapsed and a reckoning is approaching.

The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes.

grh_d1daf4936ebb0db9d67e.title: The Veteran Comes Back
paragraphs: A dramatized discussion of Willard Waller's The Veteran Comes Back examines the political and social danger created when returning servicemen are denied work, security and respect. Historical scenes from earlier American wars, including the Bonus Expeditionary Force of 1932, are used to show how neglected veterans can become bitter and vulnerable to demagogues. A contemporary G.I. voice closes by demanding jobs, housing, education, medical care and social security so millions of returning veterans can help build a better country instead of being driven against it.

Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Ben Kagen as radio adaptor, Clifton Fadiman as host, and Jack Costello as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.a811c0d1a6efa194|Johnson's Wax]].
